subject: Post-call: Model fit + quantization tradeoffs for FinWave (next steps)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finwave.com>, Priya Rao <priya@finwave.com>
Cc: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-22T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Post-call: Model fit + quantization tradeoffs for FinWave (next steps)

Hi Alex / Priya — thanks for taking the call this morning. Quick recap and recommended next steps so we can align on a POC and procurement timeline.

Call recap (30m):
- FinWave goals: replace on-prem transformer inference for customer support triage and document summarization; latency target <= 250ms p50; throughput target ~120 qps steady.
- Primary constraints: SLAs for latency, and strict quality baseline on the summarization prompts (we reviewed 20 sample prompts).
- Team: Alex (platform lead), Priya (product owner). Internal: Marissa (AE), Nikhil (SE), Lauren (AM).

Model-fit & quantization notes (summary):
- Recommended starting models: Redwood-13B-vanilla (FP16 baseline) for quality baseline; Redwood-13B-AWQ and Redwood-7B-GPTQ as lower-cost/high-throughput variants for evaluation.
- Tradeoffs we discussed: AWQ tends to give the best throughput uplift vs GPTQ (observed ~2x on our internal kernels) but can show small quality deltas on edge-case prompts; GPTQ is more predictable across prompts but slightly lower throughput; FP8 variants (where supported) can yield similar throughput to AWQ with slightly better numerical fidelity but require extra validation in your stack.

Attachments I shared: redwood-quant-trade-study.pdf (high-level AWQ/GPTQ/FP8 trade study), prompt-set-v1.csv (the 20 sample prompts we used). Also linking benchmark dashboard and the HubSpot deal below.

Proposed next steps:
1) We will share the trade study + prompt set (attached). Please run the prompt set against any internal golden prompts you want to prioritize and share the outputs — we can run side-by-side diffs.
2) SE POC: Nikhil can provision a 5-day POC environment with the three variants (FP16 baseline, AWQ, GPTQ) so you can validate latency/throughput and run your gold prompts.
3) Timeline: if you confirm POC by EOD Friday, we can spin up infra early next week. Procurement: Lauren to follow up on pricing options and reserved capacity offers.

Open questions from the call (so we don't lose them):
- Which prompt subset do you want prioritized beyond the attached 20?
- Any hard constraints on token limits or response truncation behavior?
- Are there internal metrics you need us to surface in the POC (e.g., per-token cost, latency percentiles, token-level attribution)?

Thanks — attaching the trade study and prompts now. I'll put a short mutual action plan in a follow-up.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. A few quick clarifying Qs before we commit to the POC: 

1) Quality regressions: you mentioned small deltas on edge-case prompts for AWQ. Can you quantify that delta vs FP16 (e.g., BLEU/ROUGE or human-annotated pass/fail on our 20 prompts)?
2) Latency/throughput: can you provide the p50/p95 numbers you saw for AWQ and GPTQ at ~120 qps? We need to make sure the POC config can meet <250ms p50.
3) Procurement: our procurement team needs an estimate for a 30-day reserved test. Lauren — can you provide a sketched price?

We also have one more golden prompt set (legal-doc summarization) — I'll attach it in a follow-up. If AWQ shows even a 1—132% drop in fidelity on that set, we'll need to be conservative.

Appreciate the next-step plan. If you can get the SE POC available next week, that would be ideal.

—Alex

Cc: Priya Rao <priya@finwave.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Post-call: Model fit + quantization tradeoffs for FinWave (next steps)

Alex / team — quick technical notes from our internal trade runs (see attached PDF and drive link for raw benches):

Summary (short):
- FP16 baseline (Redwood-13B)
  - Quality: baseline (0% delta) on our human evals.
  - Latency @ 120 qps (single-AZ, G5x16-ish equivalent): p50 ~ 180ms, p95 ~ 320ms (batching & KV cache dependent).
- AWQ (13B-AWQ)
  - Throughput: ~2.0—12.3x improvement in token/sec vs FP16 on same HW using our AWQ kernels.
  - Quality: observed median ~0.5—1.8% drop on our rouge-like summarization metric across the 20-sample set; failure modes concentrated on highly technical/legal language.
  - Notes: AWQ needs per-model calibration of per-layer scales; we recommend running a representative prompt set you care about to validate.
- GPTQ (7B-GPTQ and 13B-GPTQ variants)
  - Throughput: ~1.5—1.8x vs FP16 on our kernels.
  - Quality: typically closer to FP16 than AWQ on a per-prompt basis for our workloads, but less throughput uplift.
- FP8 (experimental / vendor-dependent)
  - Throughput: similar to AWQ in some runs; better numeric fidelity in ours for long-context cases.
  - Caveats: FP8 paths require validated operator kernels in your infra and may not be available on every config.

Engineering recommendations for the POC:
- Run the gold prompt sets you care about (we'll included prompt-set-v1.csv). We recommend adding your legal-doc set.
- We'll provision 3 variants in the POC: Redwood-13B-FP16 (baseline), Redwood-13B-AWQ (high-throughput), Redwood-7B-GPTQ (cost-focused).
- Nikhil can instrument the POC with per-prompt diffs, p50/p95 latency, and per-token cost breakdown.

Some quick numbers from our internal bench (approx):
- Redwood-13B-FP16: 120 qps sustained -> p50 175—1200ms
- Redwood-13B-AWQ: 240 qps sustained -> p50 85—1110ms
- Redwood-7B-GPTQ: 200 qps sustained -> p50 95—1130ms

These numbers assume continuous batching and our KV cache warm; real-world will vary depending on prompt length and sequence length.

Action I can take right now: provision a short-lived POC cluster and upload a per-prompt diff report for the 20-sample set + your legal-set once you send it. If you want, we'll also run a small human-check on the top 10 failure cases to quantify user-visible regressions.

—Nikhil
Nikhil Sharma

Mutual action plan (short):
- This week (by Fri EOD): FinWave to confirm POC prompts (attach legal-doc set) and preferred region.
- Day 0—1—1 POC spin: Redwood SE (Nikhil) provisions 5-day POC cluster with 3 variants and uploads initial bench.
- Day 2—1—4: FinWave runs prioritized prompts; Redwood runs side-by-side diffs + small human-check on top failure cases.
- Day 5: Joint review meeting to decide which quantized variant meets your quality bar for expansion.

Lauren — can you share a 30-day reserved test price and a short note on committed capacity discounts? (cc'd)

A few risk mitigations we propose if AWQ shows small regressions:
- Fallback routing: route high-risk prompts to FP16 for finalization, low-risk to AWQ for cost savings.
- Prompt-level tagging: we can add a quick metadata flag during inference to enforce FP16 for marked prompts.
- Calibration pass: we can run a short re-calibration on AWQ weights using a small representative sample to reduce outlier regressions.

Attached: redwood-quant-trade-study.pdf, prompt-set-v1.csv. HubSpot / deal: https://hubspot.redwood.ai/deal/fw-358

Can you confirm the legal-doc set by EOD Friday and we'll get the POC scheduled?

Thanks — looking forward.
